sourceNote: Compiled from public dupe-community consensus: multi-source-corroborated pairings are tagged 'strong-consensus' or 'contested'; pairings sourced from a single curated house dupe list are tagged 'contested' (stated plainly by the source) or 'loose' (the source itself hedged with 'very similar to'). Price is exact where sourced, otherwise a house-range estimate flagged 'priceEstimated'. This is a real, growing dataset, not an exhaustive catalog — full houses run 300-460+ SKUs each; see refresh_pipeline.py for the path to scale further. Houses added on request (Rayhaan, Khadlaj, Arabiyat Prestige, Mykonos, Velixir, Gulf Orchid, Maison Asrar, Fragrance World, French Avenue, Zimaya, Ahmed Al Maghribi, Afnan, Paris Corner, Bin Bujairami) are now in the house directory even where no verified pairing was found yet — those show as houses with an empty catalog rather than being silently omitted or filled with invented pairings. Beauty House (beautyhouse.com) added as a source for newer/trending releases with note pyramids and live pricing. PerfumeBox, Gift Express, and FragFlex were checked but sell authentic designer fragrances rather than publishing dupe-pairing content, so no pairings were sourced from them. Triple Traders (tripletraders.com, a real Bridgeview IL retailer) is a straight product catalog rather than an editorial dupe list — useful for confirming stock and pricing, not for new pairings. Smell-A-Likes.com added as a source — a genuine multi-reviewer crowdsourced site (dated, independent user reviews per pairing) rather than a single editorial voice, which is why a few entries here (Ard Al Zaafaran Midnight Oud, Rasasi Rumz Al Rasasi 9325) could be upgraded to 'strong-consensus' on real corroboration rather than an author's say-so. ScentClones.com added as a source for genuinely recent (dated changelog) releases with less-common inspirations — French Avenue, Dumont, and Atralia entered the dataset through this source. Note this site's marketing language ('Beast Mode', a paid '$5 roadmap' upsell) reads as commercial content; pairings are tagged 'contested' (single-source) accordingly, not elevated on the strength of the site's own accuracy-percentage claims. TikTok-trend roundups (Fragrantix, Palisade Scents) added for currently-trending pairings. Two genuine source contradictions were found and flagged in place (Maison Alhambra Liam Grey; Lattafa Ramz Lattafa Silver) rather than silently resolved in favor of one source. Khadlaj coverage expanded systematically via Fragrantica review mining (Le Prestige and Karus collections) at the user's request — this is an ongoing collection-by-collection pass, not a complete catalog audit; 219 total Khadlaj SKUs exist and most remain unchecked. Zimaya confirmed via Fragrantica editorial as an official Afnan sub-brand. Coverage expanded via the same Fragrantica-review-mining process used for Khadlaj, at the user's request. Zimaya founding details confirmed (2023, founder/perfumer Imran Fazlani). Zimaya coverage pushed to a larger batch (~30 total entries by this point) across nearly every named sub-collection at the user's request — Paragon, Sharaf, Reverie, Al Barari, Infrad, and others. Several genuine source disagreements (Infrad Noir, Sharaf the Club, Reverie Petals, Mazaaj Rhythm) were flagged rather than resolved. Gissah Imperial Valley emerged as a heavily-duped reference during Gulf Orchid research — at least four different houses (Gulf Orchid Riwaya, Paris Corner Khayr, Surrati Dream Valley, French Avenue Sultan the Founder) target it, discovered via a single fragrance-shop employee's in-store comparison account rather than four separate searches. Montagne Parfums (USA) added on user request — flagged as outside the original Middle Eastern scope of this project, included regardless since the user directed research here. Uses the same first-party 'INSPIRED BY' storefront labeling pattern as Bujairami.

houses.name: Lattafa Perfumes
houses.packagingNote: Ornate crystal-style bottles with gold-tone caps are the house signature — flagships like Khamrah and Ana Abiyedh Rouge lean into heavier, faceted glass built to look shelf-worthy next to niche houses.

houses.name: Maison Alhambra
houses.packagingNote: Explicitly built around the 'total experience' — bottle and box design frequently mirrors the exact silhouette of the niche house it references, down to cap shape and box texture.

houses.name: Armaf
houses.packagingNote: Understated compared to the crystal-heavy houses — clean rectangular bottles, brushed-metal caps, closer in presentation register to mainstream designer packaging than to ornate Arabic perfumery.

houses.name: Al Haramain Perfumes
houses.packagingNote: Known for oversized, heavily faceted bottles in the Amber Oud line — deliberately displayed as statement pieces rather than tucked away.

houses.name: Swiss Arabian
houses.packagingNote: One of the older houses in the category — bottle design trends more traditional/attar-adjacent than the crystal-cut maximalism of newer entrants.

houses.name: Paris Corner
houses.packagingNote: Entry-level packaging across most of the catalog.

houses.name: Khadlaj
houses.packagingNote: Mid-tier presentation with occasional standout releases (Island Dreams) that lean into brighter, more contemporary bottle design than the traditional Arabic-perfumery look.
houses.catalogSize: 219 (per Beauty House's full collection listing; only a handful have documented designer-dupe attribution — most of the line is original Khadlaj perfumery, not marketed as clones)

houses.name: Rasasi
houses.packagingNote: Long-established Saudi/UAE house — solid, traditional bottle design, less focused on niche-mimicry than Maison Alhambra.

houses.name: Ajmal
houses.packagingNote: One of the more heritage-positioned houses — bottle design often nods to classical Arabic perfumery motifs rather than Western niche silhouettes.

houses.name: Al Wataniah
houses.packagingNote: Modest, functional presentation.

houses.name: Arabiyat Prestige
houses.packagingNote: Positioned as a value-forward sub-line — presentation is clean but not a collector centerpiece.

houses.name: Afnan Perfumes
houses.packagingNote: Known for closely mirroring niche-house bottle silhouettes (Supremacy line in particular echoes Amouage/Nishane-style presentation).

houses.name: Zimaya
houses.packagingNote: Confirmed via Fragrantica editorial as an Afnan sub-brand, not just community speculation. Uses pre-made fragrance oil bases rather than commissioning original perfumer work, per the same source.

houses.name: Rayhaan
houses.packagingNote: Founded by Khalid Kalsekar, son of Rasasi's Salim Kalsekar — positioned under an 'Essential Luxury' banner with premium bottle detailing.

houses.name: Mykonos
houses.packagingNote: Viral Indonesian dupe house, known for stylish presentation; expanding to UK distribution via Fragrance Forte as of 2026. Notably difficult to buy at retail price due to high demand/markup, per multiple reviewers.

houses.name: Velixir
houses.packagingNote: Greek-mythology-themed naming (Ares, Apollo, Athena, Icarus, etc). Distinctive flattened egg-shaped bottle design that sits upside down on its cap — praised by reviewers as one of the more unique bottle designs in the category.

houses.name: Gulf Orchid
houses.packagingNote: Parent group to Maison Asrar; own-name releases (Mango Ice, Matcha Latte) lean into playful, contemporary bottle design.

houses.name: Maison Asrar
houses.packagingNote: Confirmed via Parfumo as marketed by Gulf Orchid Fragrances. One reviewer specifically praises the Belgravia bottle as 'nice and classy, unlike every other Middle Eastern bottle' — suggests above-average presentation investment relative to peers.

houses.name: French Avenue
houses.packagingNote: Operates as a niche-adjacent sub-line (associated with Fragrance World); leans toward rarer/less-duped niche references rather than the usual Aventus/BR540 targets.

houses.name: Ahmed Al Maghribi
houses.packagingNote: Known primarily for attars/oil concentrates alongside spray formats — no verified spray-fragrance pairing data sourced yet.

houses.name: Bin Bujairami
houses.packagingNote: Publishes explicit 'X Inspired by Y [Brand]' product titles directly on their own storefront — a first-party source rather than community speculation, though still single-sourced (their own claim) unless independently corroborated.
houses.catalogSize: 1081 products in the 'Inspired' collection alone, per the brand's own site

houses.name: Riiffs
houses.packagingNote: No verified packaging reputation sourced yet.

houses.name: Ard Al Zaafaran
houses.packagingNote: Budget-tier house; presentation is functional rather than a display centerpiece, per community sourcing.

houses.name: Dumont
houses.packagingNote: No verified packaging reputation sourced yet.

houses.name: Atralia
houses.packagingNote: No verified packaging reputation sourced yet. (Resolves an earlier uncertain 'Atrailia' name mention — confirmed as Atralia.)

houses.name: Surrati
houses.packagingNote: No verified packaging reputation sourced yet.

houses.name: Montagne Parfums
houses.packagingNote: NOT Middle Eastern — flagged for the record, since this dataset was scoped to ME clone houses. American (NYC-based) dupe house, self-described as 'Fine fragrances inspirations. Handcrafted in NYC.' Publishes explicit 'INSPIRED BY [designer]' titles directly on their own site, same pattern as Bujairami.

houses.name: Dua Fragrances
houses.catalogSize: 1000+ in the Designer Line alone, plus Inspired Expression/Hybrid/Tribrid/Quadbrid lines
houses.packagingNote: Publishes explicit 'Inspiration: X by Y' labeling directly on every product listing — a first-party source, consistent in format across the entire catalog. All fragrances made in extrait de parfum concentration (33% oil) per the brand. Also releases 'Hybrid/Tribrid/Quadbrid' products explicitly blending 2-4 designer references at once rather than targeting a single fragrance.

houses.name: Jo Milano Paris
houses.catalogSize: 58 (per Fragrantica), organized into Luxury/Diamond (Game of Spades)/Prestige/Zodiac/786/Classic collections
houses.priceRange: $80-$320 (higher-tier presentation than most houses in this dataset)
houses.packagingNote: The 'Game of Spades' (Diamond Collection) line uses playing-card-themed names (King, Queen, Royale, Diamond, Full House, Bluff) rather than naming the target directly on their own site — inspiration data for this house comes from Fragrantica community reviews, not first-party retailer labeling. Multiple reviewers independently rate this collection's quality above typical budget dupe houses.

houses.name: Volaré
houses.packagingNote: From the house of Mamlakat Al Oud (est. 1994). A genuinely new brand (Fragrantica's earliest listing is 2023), already carried by multiple third-party retailers who append shorthand nicknames for the designer target directly in product titles.

houses.name: Alexandria Fragrances
houses.packagingNote: No verified packaging reputation sourced yet beyond a customer noting quick, tracked delivery.

houses.name: CA Perfume
houses.packagingNote: Body-oil and fragrance-oil format alongside sprays, marketed as 'HumanSafe Verified.' No independent reputation sourced yet beyond product listings.

houses.name: Fragrance World
houses.packagingNote: Trading roots in Dubai's Deira market since 1988; the Fragrance World brand itself established 2004. One of the largest UAE clone/inspired-style houses, with production facilities distributing to 150+ countries.

Sourced from marketing/promotional content ('social clips frame it as a God of Fire-inspired affordable pick') rather than a direct independent reviewer comparison — treated as a weaker source than a Fragrantica/Parfumo review.

entries.inspiration: Petit Matin (primary) / Neroli Portofino (secondary hybrid element)
entries.note: Exceptionally well sourced: two independent reviewers across two platforms (Fragrantica, Parfumo) converge on the same ~85% Petit Matin / ~15% Neroli Portofino split, and one reviewer reports bringing the bottle into a Nordstrom MFK counter, where the brand's own representative confirmed it smelled much closer to Petit Matin than to Neroli Portofino. One of the best-corroborated pairings in this entire dataset.

Multiple independent reviewers converge on this reference across two separate product pages (its own reviews plus a cross-mention on Mykonos California Club), one calling it 'Invictus Parfum at half the price.'

CORRECTED: the previous entry (Invictus Parfum) was a misattribution — that claim actually came from a 'sidenote' within a California Club review that was commenting on a separate product, California Blue, not California Club itself. The real evidence for California Club points to Creed Silver Mountain Water: multiple Fragrantica reviewers state it directly ('Solid SMW dupe, boozy powdery freshie'; 'reminds me of a very synthetic and watered down Silver Mountain Water'), plus a TikTok video framing it explicitly as an SMW alternative.

entries.inspiration: Oriana (settled candidate) / Love Don't Be Shy (alternate candidate raised by the same source)
entries.note: A blog reviewer relays that 'Fragrantica and other YouTube reviewers' compared it to both Kilian's Love Don't Be Shy and Parfums de Marly's Oriana, then settles on describing it as an Oriana dupe — secondhand sourcing, not a direct review link.

Single detailed Parfumo reviewer states directly it 'clearly carries the DNA of Allure Homme Sport Superleggera,' estimating a maximum 80% similarity, with woody notes weaker than expected and musk/patchouli more prominent.

entries.inspiration: Blue Talisman (per one source) / Shaghaf Oud Tonka, Swiss Arabian (per a separate source)
entries.note: Two reviewers on two platforms name two unrelated references: a Parfumo reviewer says it 'captures the Blue Talisman DNA surprisingly well,' while a Fragrantica reviewer instead compares it to Swiss Arabian's Shaghaf Oud Tonka ('exactly like Shaghaf Oud Tonka but better blended'), which is itself a clone-house product, not the same target. Genuinely conflicting sourcing, flagged rather than resolved. Velixir was founded by two brothers from Jakarta as an Indonesian house, per a detailed brand profile.

Extremely well corroborated — Rayhaan's most-reviewed product by far (600+ ratings on Parfumo). Multiple reviewers state it directly, one calling it a fragrance that 'renders both the original VIW and current reformulation absolutely redundant,' another explicitly correcting a fellow reviewer's confusion with a different reference.

Confirmed directly by the user, aligning with the majority of independent reviewers who referenced Dior Homme Intense/Parfum ('DHI 2025', 'DHP 2014'). The competing JPG Ultra Male comparison some reviewers raised is dropped — the same reviewer who brought it up hedged on ever smelling the real Dior Homme Intense, and another reviewer had already called the Ultra Male read a 'genuine delusion.'

entries.inspiration: Near-identical to Rayhaan Obsidian (per direct reviewer comparison), now confirmed as Dior Homme Intense
entries.note: One reviewer directly compares it to Rayhaan Obsidian ('identical... impossible to tell the difference'), a sibling product now confirmed in this dataset as a Dior Homme Intense dupe. A separate reviewer instead called Lion itself 'very close to JPG Ultra Male' — that claim wasn't addressed directly and is kept as the unresolved part of this entry.

Strongly corroborated across multiple reviewers ('emulates Naxos almost perfectly,' 'the Naxos DNA is unmistakably captured'), though one dissenting reviewer instead ties it to JPG Elixir/Rayhaan Elixir. Majority view kept as primary given the volume of independent Naxos confirmations.

Multiple reviewers converge on this reference, one giving a detailed comparison ('sharper and projects further, with a distinctive tea-ish bitter note... that said, the resemblance is definitely there'). A second Halfeti dupe now confirmed in this dataset alongside Lattafa Mohra.

Exceptionally well sourced: one reviewer describes bringing a test strip to Neiman Marcus, spraying the real Dries Van Noten Santal Greenery for comparison, then having a sales associate correctly identify which card held the original when asked — describing them as '99% similar' on paper. Cross-referenced against Dua Brands' competing 'Green Sandalwood' as another dupe of the same reference.

Confirmed directly by the user, corroborating the original reviewer mention. Still kept at contested rather than strong-consensus since the underlying public reviews remain hedged ('never tried the original so cannot comment on how similar they are').

Multiple reviewers converge, one noting it's slightly sweeter and less deep than the original but close enough that most people wouldn't notice the difference on skin, another recommending people smell the real thing at Sephora first to judge fit.

Same target as the house's own Valhalla X Legion, but a starkly different quality assessment: one detailed reviewer calls it 'a very wide miss' if that's really the intended reference, listing it among four Rayhaan releases they'd skip.

Very strongly corroborated — one reviewer calls it 'the best, most beautiful, and most complete clone ever made for LV's Afternoon Swim,' another quantifies it at 85-90% close. Often overshadowed by its sibling release Pacific Aura (a Pacific Chill dupe, already in this dataset), which launched alongside it.

A detailed reviewer directly compares the two, confirming the opening is 'pretty much exactly the same' as the Armani original. A second reviewer separately compares it to Replica By The Fireplace (Maison Margiela) as being 'in the same ballpark' — a secondary reference point rather than a competing claim.

Two independent reviewers on two platforms both name this exact niche reference — one having tested the real Guerlain in-store before purchasing this as an alternative. An uncommon, specific target to see two people converge on independently.
Multiple reviewers converge, one describing a real-world blind test: a coworker 'big in perfume' who owns a bottle of the Chanel original asked if that's what they were wearing.

Real dispute: some reviewers call it 'a perfect Aventus dupe,' while others explicitly argue 'if this is supposed to be a Creed Aventus clone it's a wide miss... fruitiness isn't even close,' instead comparing it to Aventus-adjacent originals like Montblanc Explorer and Al Haramain L'Aventure rather than a direct clone.

entries.inspiration: Iberian Leather (primary candidate) — also compared to Gucci Guilty Absolute and a Black Afgano/Berlin Soul/Air Tiger blend by other reviewers
entries.note: Genuinely muddled: one detailed reviewer calls it 'an excellent inspiration of Memo's Iberian Leather... smells just like that,' another instead compares it to Gucci Guilty Absolute, and a third names three different niche references without settling on one. Iberian Leather kept as the clearest single candidate given it's the only positive direct match, but flagged as unresolved.

A detailed Spanish-language reviewer states it's 'very similar to Centaurus de Creed,' having tested the original directly. Also loosely compared by other reviewers to the house's own Terra and to Lattafa Khamrah Qahwa on general style, though those are vibe comparisons rather than direct dupe claims.
Single reviewer states directly this is 'Calvin Klein's Eternity for W clone' — not yet independently corroborated.

Multiple reviewers converge, one quantifying it at '85% close,' another describing it as 'a slightly spicier version of Oud Wood.' One of the cheapest entries in this dataset relative to its $200+ target.

Multiple reviewers converge on this niche reference, one describing an actual side-by-side wear test (Caden on one wrist, Pharaoh on the other): '80% similar at the top, 95% once it dries down.' Omanluxury Caden is now confirmed duped by at least two different houses in this dataset (also see Bujairami's Golden Souq).

A direct retailer review states plainly: 'this is definitely a dupe of Davidoff Cool Water.' Worth flagging clearly: despite the similar 'Wave'/'Aqua' branding and packaging, this appears to target a different reference than Pacific Aura (Pacific Chill) — the two shouldn't be assumed interchangeable.

A third, separate Aqua Collection product (distinct from both Pacific Aura and Fresh Wave). Multiple reviewers converge directly: 'first spray and I thought it was Invictus — probably one of the best smelling Invictus dupes I have smelled so far.'

Very strongly corroborated across multiple platforms — a Fragrantica reviewer who owns the $350+ Byredo original calls it 'over 90% similar,' a dedicated YouTube review titled directly around the comparison, and a TikTok caption stating it explicitly as 'inspired by Mojave Ghost Absolu.'

Confirmed via a dedicated YouTube review titled explicitly 'Cedrus Blanc a clone of Carolina Herrera Cedar Chic,' plus a TikTok caption naming the same pairing directly. Released as a companion pair alongside Nava Sol (Mojave Ghost Absolu).

About as strong a cross-source consensus as exists in this category — named the top Aventus dupe independently by at least seven separate review sites and blogs (Scento, Off The Record, PickMyClone, Palette21, Tonkava, ScentCritic, ScentClones), several explicitly calling it 'the gold standard' or 'undisputed champion' for accuracy and value. One source cites a 98/100 community validation score, the highest of any Aventus alternative tested. Common critique across sources: a sharp, synthetic citrus opening in the first 15-30 minutes that settles into a much closer dry-down.

Named the top-ranked Green Irish Tweed alternative by one review site (90/100, 'the strongest starting point for most shoppers'), scored on how faithfully it rebuilds the verbena-violet-woods structure. A separate independent tester instead named Armaf Tres Nuit their top pick at a similar accuracy score — genuine disagreement on which is actually best, not just a matter of degree.

Named the top Silver Mountain Water dupe by multiple independent sources (PerfumeCloneFinder rates it highest at 8.5/10, The Scent File scores it 8/10 community accuracy, multiple TikTok comparisons favor it over Afnan Supremacy In Heaven). Competing candidates exist from other sources — Rasasi Al Wisam Day and ALT Platinum Water were each independently named 'closest match' by separate review sites — but Armaf's pick has the most independent corroboration of any single option.

Named independently by two separate review sites (FragranceReview.com, Besuited Aroma) as one of the closer Virgin Island Water clones, both noting it swaps the original's rum/sugarcane base for woody notes and sweet musk — a deliberate deviation reviewers say works if you don't need the signature boozy base.

First-party claim from Dua's own product copy ('inspired expression of Creed's Erolfa'), with one reviewer even calling it possibly better than the original. Worth flagging honestly: a dedicated Fragrantica forum thread asking for an Erolfa dupe found genuine community skepticism that a good one exists at all — one poster who tried a different clone called it 'terrible, nothing similar to Erolfa.'

Named the top Himalaya clone by one rating site (82% accuracy score) — but two other independent sources instead name Alexandria's Himalaya Mountains and a small house called Ree Fragrances' Alaska Winter as their respective top picks. Genuine disagreement, no clear community consensus winner for this reference.

Named 'the best option' for a Himalaya clone by one review site, describing it as toned-down/lighter than the original but structurally similar. A competing source instead named Dua's Everest their top pick — no clear consensus winner across sources for this reference.

Well corroborated for a house typically at contested tier — a dedicated comparison blog post concludes the two are 'more alike than different,' multiple Parfumo reviewers independently confirm ('the drydown is 100% identical'), and there's a dedicated YouTube side-by-side review. The most genuine clone-house pick found for this reference — most other 'similar to Bois du Portugal' recommendations point to unrelated designer fragrances (Lalique Pour Homme, Guerlain Heritage) that aren't deliberate dupes and don't belong in this dataset.

Confirmed via first-party product listing ('Inspired by Creed Royal Mayfair'), the same pine/gin/lime/rose/eucalyptus/cedar note profile as the original. Worth flagging honestly: at time of research this specific product showed only a single customer review, rated 1.0/5 — genuinely thin and unfavorable evidence, not a reason for confidence despite the clear first-party sourcing.

Confirmed by the user (as 'Bianca Pura'). Well-sourced beyond the first-party listing — an independent Parfumo reviewer calls it 'an affordable alternative to Creed's Pure White Cologne,' two separate YouTube videos do direct real-vs-clone side-by-side comparisons, and a resale listing independently describes it as a 'clone of Creed's Pure White.' Also has a companion hybrid, Bleu Bianca Pura, which explicitly blends this with a vintage Bleu de Chanel formulation.
